sanskrit: tasya caiva samabhyāśe nikṣipyāṇḍāni sarvaśaḥ samudrāmbhasy amodanta caranto bhīṣma pakṣiṇaḥ
english: In that very vicinity, having laid their eggs everywhere, the birds roamed about joyfully in the waters of the sea, O Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: teṣām aṇḍāni sarveṣāṃ bhakṣayām āsa pāpakṛt sa haṃsaḥ saṃpramattānām apramattaḥ svakarmaṇi
english: That wicked swan devoured the eggs of all those birds — vigilant in his own doings while they were careless and inattentive.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṣīyamāṇeṣu teṣv aṇḍeṣv aṇḍajo 'paraḥ aśaṅkata mahāprājñas taṃ kadā cid dadarśa ha
english: Then, as those eggs were steadily diminishing, another bird born of an egg — a wise and vigilant one — grew suspicious and one day happened to catch sight of him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kathayām āsa dṛṣṭvā haṃsasya kilbiṣam teṣāṃ paramaduḥkhārtaḥ sa pakṣī sarvapakṣiṇām
english: Then that bird, overcome with the deepest grief on behalf of all birds, reported the sinful deed of the swan to them after witnessing it.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyakṣato dṛṣṭvā pakṣiṇas te samāgatāḥ nijaghnus taṃ tadā haṃsaṃ mithyāvṛttaṃ kurūdvaha
english: Then those birds, assembling together and seeing it with their own eyes, killed that swan who had behaved so falsely, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: te tvāṃ haṃsasadharmāṇam apīme vasudhādhipāḥ nihanyur bhīṣma saṃkruddhāḥ pakṣiṇas tam ivāṇḍajam
english: These kings of the earth too, O Bhīṣma, may slay you — who are of the same nature as that swan — just as those furious birds slew that egg-born creature.

sanskrit: gāthām apy atra gāyanti ye purāṇavido janāḥ bhīṣma yāṃ tāṃ ca te samyak kathayiṣyāmi bhārata
english: Those who are versed in the ancient lore also sing a verse on this matter, O Bhīṣma — that verse I shall relate to you accurately, O Bharata.

sanskrit: antarātmani vinihite; rauṣi patraratha vitatham aṇḍabhakṣaṇam aśuci te; karma vācam atiśayate
english: "When the inner self is invested in wrong, O winged one, you rage falsely; the eating of eggs is impure for you — your deed surpasses your words."

sanskrit: śiśupāla uvāca sa me bahumato rājā jarāsaṃdho mahābalaḥ yo 'nena yuddhaṃ neyeṣa dāso 'yam iti saṃyuge
english: Śiśupāla said: That great and mighty king Jarāsandha is highly esteemed by me — one who refused to fight with this man in battle, saying "This one is a mere slave."

sanskrit: keśavena kṛtaṃ yat tu jarāsaṃdhavadhe tadā bhīmasenārjunābhyāṃ ca kas tat sādhv iti manyate
english: What Keśava did at the slaying of Jarāsandha, along with Bhīmasena and Arjuna — who considers that to have been a righteous act?

sanskrit: advāreṇa praviṣṭena chadmanā brahmavādinā dṛṣṭaḥ prabhāvaḥ kṛṣṇena jarāsaṃdhasya dhīmataḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa, having entered by a back way in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa speaker, witnessed for himself the power of the wise Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: yena dharmātmanātmānaṃ brahmaṇyam abhijānatā naiṣitaṃ pādyam asmai tad dātum agre durātmane
english: He who, knowing himself to be righteous and devoted to Brāhmaṇas, would not have offered the water of welcome first to that wicked-souled one.

sanskrit: bhujyatām iti tenoktāḥ kṛṣṇabhīmadhanaṃjayāḥ jarāsaṃdhena kauravya kṛṣṇena vikṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma, and Dhanañjaya were told by Jarāsandha, "Eat and be welcome" — yet Kṛṣṇa did what was improper, O Kauravya.

sanskrit: yady ayaṃ jagataḥ kartā yathainaṃ mūrkha manyase kasmān na brāhmaṇaṃ samyag ātmānam avagacchati
english: If he is truly the creator of the world, as you foolishly believe, then why does he not properly recognise himself as a Brāhmaṇa?

sanskrit: idaṃ tv āścaryabhūtaṃ me yad ime pāṇḍavās tvayā apakṛṣṭāḥ satāṃ mārgān manyante tac ca sādhv iti
english: This is what amazes me — that these Pāṇḍavas, drawn away from the path of the righteous by you, still regard it as proper.

sanskrit: atha vā naitad āścaryaṃ yeṣāṃ tvam asi bhārata strīsadharmā ca vṛddhaś ca sarvārthānāṃ pradarśakaḥ
english: Or perhaps this is no wonder, O Bharata — for you are their guide in all matters: you who are both of the nature of a woman and an old man.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rūkṣaṃ rūkṣākṣaraṃ bahu cukopa balināṃ śreṣṭho bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those harsh and rough-syllabled words of his, the glorious Bhīmasena, foremost among the strong, became exceedingly angry.

sanskrit: tasya padmapratīkāśe svabhāvāyatavistṛte bhūyaḥ krodhābhitāmrānte rakte netre babhūvatuḥ
english: His eyes — naturally wide and expansive, resembling lotus petals — grew red once more, their corners flushed deep crimson with wrath.

sanskrit: triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ cāsya dadṛśuḥ sarvapārthivāḥ lalāṭasthāṃ trikūṭasthāṃ gaṅgāṃ tripathagām iva
english: All the assembled kings beheld on his forehead a triple-ridged frown — like the triple-peaked Trikūṭa mountain, or the Gaṅgā flowing in three streams.

sanskrit: dantān saṃdaśatas tasya kopād dadṛśur ānanam yugānte sarvabhūtāni kālasyeva didhakṣataḥ
english: They saw the face of him as he ground his teeth in rage — like the face of Time at the end of an age, as he would burn all beings.

sanskrit: utpatantaṃ tu vegena jagrāhainaṃ manasvinam bhīṣma eva mahābāhur mahāsenam iveśvaraḥ
english: But as he leapt up with fierce velocity, the mighty-armed Bhīṣma seized that high-spirited one, as a lord might restrain a great general.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmasya bhīṣmeṇa vāryamāṇasya bhārata guruṇā vividhair vākyaiḥ krodhaḥ praśamam āgataḥ
english: Restrained by Bhīṣma with many varied words of counsel, O Bharata, the wrath of that Bhīma subsided.

sanskrit: nāticakrāma bhīṣmasya sa hi vākyam ariṃdamaḥ samuddhūto ghanāpāye velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: That subduer of enemies did not transgress the word of Bhīṣma — even when aroused, as the great ocean does not pass beyond the shoreline when the rains are over.

sanskrit: śiśupālas tu saṃkruddhe bhīmasene narādhipa nākampata tadā vīraḥ pauruṣe sve vyavasthitaḥ
english: But Śiśupāla, O king of men, did not tremble even when Bhīmasena grew enraged — that hero stood firm in his own manliness.

sanskrit: utpatantaṃ tu vegena punaḥ punar ariṃdamaḥ na sa taṃ cintayām āsa siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: As Bhīma leapt up again and again with furious speed, that subduer of foes paid him no regard at all — just as a lion pays no heed to a small animal.

sanskrit: prahasaṃś cābravīd vākyaṃ cedirājaḥ pratāpavān bhīmasenam atikruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmaparākramam
english: Laughing, the glorious king of Cedi spoke these words upon seeing the exceedingly wrathful Bhīmasena, whose prowess is terrible.

sanskrit: muñcainaṃ bhīṣma paśyantu yāvad enaṃ narādhipāḥ matpratāpāgninirdagdhaṃ pataṃgam iva vahninā
english: "Release him, Bhīṣma — let the kings of the earth watch as he is consumed by the fire of my prowess, like a moth by a flame."

sanskrit: tataś cedipater vākyaṃ tac chrutvā kurusattamaḥ bhīmasenam uvācedaṃ bhīṣmo matimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, having heard those words of the king of Cedi, the foremost of the Kurus — Bhīṣma, best among the wise — spoke thus to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca cedirājakule jātas tryakṣa eṣa caturbhujaḥ rāsabhārāvasadṛśaṃ rurāva ca nanāda ca
english: Bhīṣma said: This one was born in the royal line of Cedi with three eyes and four arms, and he brayed and roared with a sound like that of a donkey.

sanskrit: tenāsya mātāpitarau tresatus tau sabāndhavau vaikṛtaṃ tac ca tau dṛṣṭvā tyāgāya kurutāṃ matim
english: By that, his mother and father, along with all the kinsmen, were terrified; and seeing that ill omen, the two of them resolved to abandon him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāryaṃ nṛpatiṃ sāmātyaṃ sapurohitam cintāsaṃmūḍhahṛdayaṃ vāg uvācāśarīriṇī
english: Then a disembodied voice addressed the king with his wife, his ministers, and his priest — whose hearts were bewildered with anxiety.

sanskrit: eṣa te nṛpate putraḥ śrīmāñ jāto mahābalaḥ tasmād asmān na bhetavyam avyagraḥ pāhi vai śiśum
english: "O king, this glorious and mighty son has been born to you — do not be afraid of us; without anxiety, protect this child."

sanskrit: na caivaitasya mṛtyus tvaṃ na kālaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ mṛtyur hantāsya śastreṇa sa cotpanno narādhipa
english: "You are not this one's death, nor has his time come yet; his killer will slay him with a weapon, and that killer has already been born, O king."

sanskrit: saṃśrutyodāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ bhūtam antarhitaṃ tataḥ putrasnehābhisaṃtaptā jananī vākyam abravīt
english: Having heard those words uttered by the spirit, which then vanished from sight, the mother — burning with maternal love for her son — spoke.

sanskrit: yenedam īritaṃ vākyaṃ mamaiva tanayaṃ prati prāñjalis taṃ namasyāmi bravītu sa punar vacaḥ
english: "I bow with joined palms to that being who has spoken these words concerning my own son — let him speak again."

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi putrasya ko 'sya mṛtyur bhaviṣyati antarhitaṃ tato bhūtam uvācedaṃ punar vacaḥ
english: "I wish to hear who shall be the death of my son." Then that invisible spirit spoke these words once more.

sanskrit: yenotsaṅge gṛhītasya bhujāv abhyadhikāv ubhau patiṣyataḥ kṣititale pañcaśīrṣāv ivoragau
english: "The one in whose lap this child is taken up — his two extra arms shall fall to the ground like two five-headed serpents."

sanskrit: tṛtīyam etad bālasya lalāṭasthaṃ ca locanam nimajjiṣyati yaṃ dṛṣṭvā so 'sya mṛtyur bhaviṣyati
english: "And this third eye on the child's forehead shall sink away; the one upon seeing whom that happens — he shall be the death of this child."

sanskrit: tryakṣaṃ caturbhujaṃ śrutvā tathā ca samudāhṛtam dharaṇyāṃ pārthivāḥ sarve abhyagacchan didṛkṣavaḥ
english: Having heard that he was three-eyed and four-armed, and that such a prophecy had been made, all the kings of the earth came to see him for themselves.

sanskrit: tān pūjayitvā saṃprāptān yathārhaṃ sa mahīpatiḥ ekaikasya nṛpasyāṅke putram āropayat tadā
english: Having duly honoured those who had arrived, the lord of the earth placed the child on the lap of each king one by one.

sanskrit: evaṃ rājasahasrāṇāṃ pṛthaktvena yathākramam śiśur aṅke samārūḍho na tat prāpa nidarśanam
english: Thus the child was placed in the laps of thousands of kings one by one in order — but the prophesied sign did not occur.

sanskrit: tataś cedipuraṃ prāptau saṃkarṣaṇajanārdanau yādavau yādavīṃ draṣṭuṃ svasāraṃ tāṃ pitus tadā
english: Then the two Yādavas, Sankarshana and Janārdana, arrived at the city of Cedi to visit that Yādava woman — their father's sister.

sanskrit: abhivādya yathānyāyaṃ yathājyeṣṭhaṃ nṛpāṃś ca tān kuśalānāmayaṃ pṛṣṭvā niṣaṇṇau rāmakeśavau
english: Having duly saluted the elders in proper order and inquired after the welfare of those kings, Rāma and Keśava took their seats.

sanskrit: abhyarcitau tadā vīrau prītyā cābhyadhikaṃ tataḥ putraṃ dāmodarotsaṅge devī saṃnyadadhāt svayam
english: The two heroes having been honoured with exceeding affection, the queen herself then placed her son in the lap of Dāmodara.

sanskrit: nyastamātrasya tasyāṅke bhujāv abhyadhikāv ubhau petatus tac ca nayanaṃ nimamajja lalāṭajam
english: The very moment the child was placed in his lap, both extra arms fell off, and that eye on the forehead sank and vanished.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā vyathitā trastā varaṃ kṛṣṇam ayācata dadasva me varaṃ kṛṣṇa bhayārtāyā mahābhuja
english: Seeing that, she was distressed and frightened, and she begged a boon of Kṛṣṇa: "Grant me a boon, O Kṛṣṇa, O mighty-armed one — I am overcome with fear."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hy ārtānāṃ samāśvāso bhītānām abhayaṃkaraḥ pitṛṣvasāraṃ mā bhaiṣīr ity uvāca janārdanaḥ
english: "You are the refuge of the afflicted and the giver of fearlessness to the frightened." Janārdana said: "Do not be afraid, O father's sister."

sanskrit: dadāni kaṃ varaṃ kiṃ vā karavāṇi pitṛṣvasaḥ śakyaṃ vā yadi vāśakyaṃ kariṣyāmi vacas tava
english: "What boon shall I give, or what shall I do for you, O father's sister? Whether possible or impossible, I shall fulfil your words."

sanskrit: evam uktā tataḥ kṛṣṇam abravīd yadunandanam śiśupālasyāparādhān kṣamethās tvaṃ mahābala
english: Thus addressed, she then said to Kṛṣṇa, the joy of the Yadus: "You must pardon the offences of Śiśupāla, O mighty one."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca aparādhaśataṃ kṣāmyaṃ mayā hy asya pitṛṣvasaḥ putrasya te vadhārhāṇāṃ mā tvaṃ śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa said: A hundred offences of his I shall pardon, O father's sister — even of your son who deserves death. Do not let your mind dwell in grief.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam eṣa nṛpaḥ pāpaḥ śiśupālaḥ sumandadhīḥ tvāṃ samāhvayate vīra govindavaradarpitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus this sinful king Śiśupāla, of utterly feeble understanding, challenges you, O hero — emboldened by the boon given by Govinda himself.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca naiṣā cedipater buddhir yayā tvāhvayate 'cyutam nūnam eṣa jagadbhartuḥ kṛṣṇasyaiva viniścayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: This is not the king of Cedi's own intelligence by which he challenges the Imperishable One — surely this is none other than the will of Kṛṣṇa himself, the sustainer of the world.

sanskrit: ko hi māṃ bhīmasenādya kṣitāv arhati pārthivaḥ kṣeptuṃ daivaparītātmā yathaiṣa kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: For who among the kings of this earth could hurl insults at me — even Bhīmasena — whose soul is overcome by fate, as this disgrace to his lineage has done?

sanskrit: eṣa hy asya mahābāho tejoṃśaś ca harer dhruvam tam eva punar ādātum icchat pṛthuyaśā hariḥ
english: For this one is assuredly a part of Hari's own splendour, O mighty-armed one — and the wide-famed Hari, wishing to reclaim that portion, seeks it back.

sanskrit: yenaiṣa kuruśārdūla śārdūla iva cedirāṭ garjaty atīva durbuddhiḥ sarvān asmān acintayan
english: It is by that power that this king of Cedi, O tiger among the Kurus, roars like a tiger — that one of utterly wicked understanding, giving no thought to any of us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato na mamṛṣe caidyas tad bhīṣmavacanaṃ tadā uvāca cainaṃ saṃkruddhaḥ punar bhīṣmam athottaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king of Cedi did not tolerate those words of Bhīṣma, and enraged, he spoke these further words in reply to Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: śiśupāla uvāca dviṣatāṃ no 'stu bhīṣmaiṣa prabhāvaḥ keśavasya yaḥ yasya saṃstavavaktā tvaṃ bandivat satatotthitaḥ
english: Śiśupāla said: May this power of Keśava — whose perpetual panegyrist you are, rising up like a bard — belong to our enemies, O Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: saṃstavāya mano bhīṣma pareṣāṃ ramate sadā yadi saṃstauṣi rājñas tvam imaṃ hitvā janārdanam
english: Your mind always delights in praising others, O Bhīṣma — if you must praise kings, then praise some other king and leave off Janārdana.

sanskrit: daradaṃ stuhi bāhlīkam imaṃ pārthivasattamam jāyamānena yeneyam abhavad dāritā mahī
english: Praise the Darada, praise Bahlika — this foremost of kings, at whose very birth the earth was split asunder.

sanskrit: vaṅgāṅgaviṣayādhyakṣaṃ sahasrākṣasamaṃ bale stuhi karṇam imaṃ bhīṣma mahācāpavikarṣaṇam
english: Praise Karṇa, O Bhīṣma — the overlord of the Vanga and Aṅga regions, equal to the thousand-eyed Indra in might, the mighty stretcher of the great bow.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ drauṇiṃ ca sādhu tvaṃ pitāputrau mahārathau stuhi stutyāv imau bhīṣma satataṃ dvijasattamau
english: Rightly praise Droṇa and his son Aśvatthāmā — the father and son, both great warriors, both ever worthy of praise, O Bhīṣma, finest of twice-born men.

sanskrit: yayor anyataro bhīṣma saṃkruddhaḥ sacarācarām imāṃ vasumatīṃ kuryād aśeṣām iti me matiḥ
english: Either one of them, O Bhīṣma, if roused to anger, could reduce this entire earth — moving and unmoving — to nothing: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: droṇasya hi samaṃ yuddhe na paśyāmi narādhipam aśvatthāmnas tathā bhīṣma na caitau stotum icchasi
english: I see no king equal to Droṇa in battle, nor to Aśvatthāmā either, O Bhīṣma — yet you have no desire to praise even these two.

sanskrit: śalyādīn api kasmāt tvaṃ na stauṣi vasudhādhipān stavāya yadi te buddhir vartate bhīṣma sarvadā
english: Why do you not praise Śalya and the other lords of the earth, O Bhīṣma — if your mind is always inclined toward the giving of praise?

sanskrit: kiṃ hi śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ yad vṛddhānāṃ tvayā nṛpa purā kathayatāṃ nūnaṃ na śrutaṃ dharmavādinām
english: What can I do, O king — you who once recounted the words of the elders, the speakers of dharma, have surely not truly heard them.

sanskrit: ātmanindātmapūjā ca paranindā parastavaḥ anācaritam āryāṇāṃ vṛttam etac caturvidham
english: Self-disparagement, self-praise, the defaming of others, and the flattering of others — these four kinds of conduct are not practised by the noble.

sanskrit: yad astavyam imaṃ śaśvan mohāt saṃstauṣi bhaktitaḥ keśavaṃ tac ca te bhīṣma na kaś cid anumanyate
english: That you constantly praise this Keśava who is unworthy of such praise, through delusion and blind devotion — not a single person approves of this, O Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhojasya puruṣe vargapāle durātmani samāveśayase sarvaṃ jagat kevalakāmyayā
english: How can you place the entire world in the person of this Bhoja — a mere herdsman, a wicked soul — out of sheer partiality?

sanskrit: atha vaiṣā na te bhaktiḥ pakṛtiṃ yāti bhārata mayaiva kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ bhūliṅgaśakunir yathā
english: Or perhaps this devotion of yours does not yield to reason, O Bharata — as I have already described before, like the story of the bhulinga bird.

sanskrit: bhūliṅgaśakunir nāma pārśve himavataḥ pare bhīṣma tasyāḥ sadā vācaḥ śrūyante 'rthavigarhitāḥ
english: There is a bird called bhulinga on the far side of the Himālayas, O Bhīṣma — its words are always heard to be contrary to its own interest.

sanskrit: mā sāhasam itīdaṃ sā satataṃ vāśate kila sāhasaṃ cātmanātīva carantī nāvabudhyate
english: It constantly cries out, "Do not act rashly!" — yet itself acts with extreme rashness and does not even perceive it.

sanskrit: sā hi māṃsārgalaṃ bhīṣma mukhāt siṃhasya khādataḥ dantāntaravilagnaṃ yat tad ādatte 'lpacetanā
english: For that little-witted bird, O Bhīṣma, snatches away the morsel of flesh lodged between the teeth of a lion as it is eating.

sanskrit: icchataḥ sā hi siṃhasya bhīṣma jīvaty asaṃśayam tadvat tvam apy adharmajña sadā vācaḥ prabhāṣase
english: It lives only because the lion permits it, O Bhīṣma — make no mistake about it. In the same way, O you who are ignorant of dharma, you always speak such words.

sanskrit: icchatāṃ pārthivendrāṇāṃ bhīṣma jīvasy asaṃśayam lokavidviṣṭakarmā hi nānyo 'sti bhavatā samaḥ
english: You live only because these lords of kings allow it, O Bhīṣma — make no mistake. For there is no one else like you who performs deeds so universally despised.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataś cedipateḥ śrutvā bhīṣmaḥ sa kaṭukaṃ vacaḥ uvācedaṃ vaco rājaṃś cedirājasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having heard those bitter words of the king of Cedi, Bhīṣma spoke these words while the king of Cedi listened, O king.

sanskrit: icchatāṃ kila nāmāhaṃ jīvāmy eṣāṃ mahīkṣitām yo 'haṃ na gaṇayāmy etāṃs tṛṇānīva narādhipān
english: "Indeed it is said that I live at the pleasure of these lords of the earth — I who do not count these kings of men as worth more than blades of grass."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu bhīṣmeṇa tataḥ saṃcukrudhur nṛpāḥ ke cij jahṛṣire tatra ke cid bhīṣmaṃ jagarhire
english: When Bhīṣma had spoken thus, the kings then became enraged; some among them rejoiced, while others reproached Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: ke cid ūcur maheṣvāsāḥ śrutvā bhīṣmasya tad vacaḥ pāpo 'valipto vṛddhaś ca nāyaṃ bhīṣmo 'rhati kṣamām
english: Some of the great archers, having heard those words of Bhīṣma, said: "This Bhīṣma is sinful, arrogant, and old — he does not deserve to be forgiven."

sanskrit: hanyatāṃ durmatir bhīṣmaḥ paśuvat sādhv ayaṃ nṛpaiḥ sarvaiḥ sametya saṃrabdhair dahyatāṃ vā kaṭāgninā
english: "Let the evil-minded Bhīṣma be slain like a beast — it is proper that all the kings, massing together in fury, should kill him, or burn him in a fire of straw."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā tataḥ kurupitāmahaḥ uvāca matimān bhīṣmas tān eva vasudhādhipān
english: Having heard those words of theirs, the grandfather of the Kurus — the wise Bhīṣma — then spoke to those very lords of the earth.
